intro: To change the text insertion cursor color in the Cursor IDE on your Mac, you must add specific color customization rules to your settings.json file. You can access this file through the Command Palette to modify the editor's appearance and change cursor color on Mac systems.
tldr: Open the Command Palette with ⌘ ⇧ P.
Add the workbench.colorCustomizations object to your file.
Define your cursor colors using hex codes.
Save the file to apply changes immediately.

blocks.text: Why customize your text cursor color

The blinking text cursor is your primary indicator of where your next character will appear. On high resolution Mac displays, the default color might blend into your chosen theme. Customizing this color helps you track your position faster. This is especially useful during long coding sessions or when working with complex syntax. By changing your cursor color, you gain a visual edge that keeps you focused on your code. You do not need to install plugins to achieve this. The editor includes built-in support for these visual tweaks.

Cursor is built on the same architecture as VS Code. This means it uses a JSON file to store your user preferences. When you want to modify deep interface settings, you edit this file directly. The workbench.colorCustomizations object is the standard way to override theme colors. This method is safe and reversible. If you make a mistake, the editor will show you exactly where the syntax is invalid. You can then fix it before saving your changes.
Steps to change cursor color on Mac

Follow these steps to update your cursor appearance. Ensure you are using the latest version of Cursor. You can check for updates in the top menu bar. These settings apply globally to your editor instance. They will persist even if you switch projects or restart your Mac.

Beyond basic colors, you can also adjust the cursor style. Options include block, line, underline, and thin line. To change the style, open your settings with ⌘ , and search for Editor: Cursor Style. If you choose the block style, you can also set a background color. This creates a high contrast box around your character. Experiment with different hex codes to find what works best for your eyes. Remember that alpha channels are supported. You can add transparency to your colors by appending two extra characters to your hex code.

faq.question: Does changing the cursor color affect performance?
faq.answer: No. These visual changes are handled by the editor's UI layer and have no impact on your code execution or system speed.

faq.question: Can I have different cursor colors for different themes?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use the workbench.colorCustomizations object within your settings.json to define colors that stay consistent regardless of the theme you select.

faq.question: Where can I find more help with Cursor settings?
faq.answer: The official Cursor documentation provides a full list of available workbench customization keys that you can use to further style your environment.

task: Change the text insertion cursor color in the Cursor IDE

steps.name: Open Command Palette
steps.text: Press ⌘ ⇧ P to open the command palette in Cursor.

steps.name: Access User Settings
steps.text: Type Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON) and press Enter.

steps.name: Edit JSON
steps.text: Add the workbench.colorCustomizations block to your JSON file.
steps.tip: Ensure you put a comma after the previous line if it is not the last item.

steps.name: Save File
steps.text: Press ⌘ S to save the file and apply the changes.

troubleshooting.fix: Check for missing commas between JSON properties or invalid hex codes.
Switch to a different base theme in the preferences menu to see if the theme is overriding your color.
